lessons.title: 1.1 Divisions and Branches of Biology
lessons.notes_html:
Introduction

Biology is divided into many branches, each branch studies one part of living things. Biology is also linked with many other sciences, so it is called a multidisciplinary subject.

Important Branches of Biology

BranchWhat it studies
AnatomyThe internal structure of the bodies of organisms.
HistologyThe structure of tissues.
ImmunologyThe body's immune system and protection against diseases.
PharmacologyThe science of medicines; the effect and use of medicines are studied in it.
EntomologyThe science of insects.
BiometryBiological measurement and statistics are used in it.
BiogeographyThe geographical distribution of organisms on the Earth.
SurgeryDiseases are treated by means of operations.
Animal husbandryRearing animals, caring for them and gaining benefit from them.
PalaeontologyThe science of fossils; the age of past life is known through the study of fossils.

Classification

Dividing different organisms into different groups or kingdoms on the basis of their characteristics is called classification.

Treatment of Diseases

Diseases are treated through both the science of medicines (pharmacology) and surgery. That is why the science of the treatment of diseases includes both of them.

Agriculture and Horticulture

AgricultureHorticulture
In agriculture, crops are grown.Horticulture is the part of agriculture in which new plant varieties are produced and the growth of fruits is cared for; new plant varieties, fruits and flowers are grown in it.

Fisheries

The work of breeding good fish and increasing fish production is called fisheries. Fish is a good source of protein, because fish contains a lot of protein.

Finding the Age of Fossils

Radio-dating and carbon dating are used to find out the age of fossils. Through palaeontology, the age of all organic life can be known.

Biology and Other Sciences

Biology is called a multidisciplinary subject because it is related to many other sciences, such as physics, chemistry, mathematics and geography, and it has many branches.

Biology linked withBranch formed
PhysicsBiophysics
ChemistryBiochemistry
MathematicsBiometry
GeographyBiogeography

Biology is also related to medicine, agriculture and other fields.

How Biology Serves Farmers

  • By increasing crop production.
  • By producing new plant varieties.
  • By controlling pests.
  • By improving animal rearing.

New plant varieties are produced through selection, grafting and genetic methods.

Contribution of Muslim Scientists

Muslim scientists made a great contribution to biology. Scientists of Europe also benefited from their books.

  • Jabir bin Hayyan worked in chemistry.
  • Ibn Sina worked in medicine.
  • Al-Razi worked in skin diseases and smallpox-measles.
  • Al-Biruni and others worked in botany and zoology.

mcqs.q: What is the breeding of good fish and fish production called?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is fisheries. The source answer states that breeding good fish and increasing fish production is called fisheries, while horticulture is about plants and fruits.

mcqs.q: With the help of which science can the age of all organic life be known?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is palaeontology, the science of fossils. The age of past life is known through the study of fossils, not through the study of insects or tissues.

mcqs.q: What is anatomy?
options: The science of the internal structure of the bodies of organisms
The science of the geographical distribution of organisms
mcqs.why: Anatomy is the science in which the internal structure of the bodies of organisms is studied. The science of insects is entomology and the science of medicines is pharmacology.

mcqs.q: What is histology?
options: The science of measurement and statistics
The science of the structure of tissues
mcqs.why: Histology is the science in which the structure of tissues is studied. It does not deal with fossils, operations or statistics, which belong to other branches.

mcqs.q: The science of the treatment of diseases includes which of the following?
mcqs.why: Diseases are treated through both the science of medicines, which is pharmacology, and surgery. Choosing only one of them gives an incomplete answer, so both together is correct.

mcqs.q: What is entomology?
options: The science of the immune system
mcqs.why: Entomology is the science of insects. The study of tissues is histology and the study of the immune system is immunology, so those options do not fit here.

mcqs.q: What is biogeography?
options: The science of the geographical distribution of organisms on the Earth
mcqs.why: Biogeography is the science in which the geographical distribution of organisms on the Earth is studied. It is the branch formed when biology is linked with geography.

mcqs.q: How is horticulture different from agriculture?
options: In horticulture only fish are bred
In horticulture diseases are treated by operations
Horticulture is the part of agriculture for new plant varieties and the growth of fruits
Horticulture is the study of fossils
mcqs.why: In agriculture crops are grown in general, while horticulture is its part in which new plant varieties are produced and the growth of fruits is cared for.

mcqs.q: Why is biology called a multidisciplinary subject?
options: Because it is studied in only one language
Because it is related to many other sciences such as physics, chemistry, mathematics and geography, and has many branches
Because it deals only with animals
mcqs.why: Biology is related to physics as biophysics, to chemistry as biochemistry, to mathematics as biometry and to geography as biogeography. These many links and branches make it multidisciplinary.

mcqs.q: Which Muslim scientist worked on skin diseases and smallpox-measles?
mcqs.why: According to the source, Al-Razi worked in skin diseases and smallpox-measles. Jabir bin Hayyan worked in chemistry and Ibn Sina worked in medicine.

lessons.title: 1.2 Levels of Organisation
lessons.notes_html:
Bio-elements: The Basis of Organisation

Bio-elements are the elements necessary for life, such as carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus and sulphur. The elements necessary for life are found in all living things.

  • The six basic elements are: carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus and sulphur.
  • A statement that leaves out sulphur from these six elements is incomplete, so it is a wrong statement.

The basis of life rests on protoplasm. Protoplasm is the chemical basis of life.

The Levels of Organisation

The levels of organisation run from small to large, and each larger level is made of the smaller levels:

Atom → molecule → cell → tissue → organ → system → organism → population → community → ecosystem → biosphere

  • Similar cells together make a tissue.
  • The correct order of biological organisation begins: atom → molecule → cell → tissue → organ.

Species, Population and Community

LevelEasy meaning
SpeciesA species is recognised when its members can interbreed and produce fertile offspring.
PopulationA group of organisms of the same species living together in one place is called a population.
CommunityMembers of different species living together at a particular place form a community.
BiosphereThe part of the Earth where life is found is called the biosphere.

Population and Community: The Difference

PopulationCommunity
A population is a group of members of one species.In a community, members of different species live together.

Colonial and Multicellular Organisation

Colonial organisationMulticellular organisation
Many cells live together but each cell does its own work, as in Volvox.Cells together form tissues, organs and systems, and the work is divided.
  • Volvox is a colony of green algae, so it is a multicellular body of green algae living in colonial organisation.
  • The scientific name of the frog is Rana tigrina.

mcqs.q: What is a group of organisms of the same species living together in one place called?
mcqs.why: Organisms of the same species living together in one place form a population. A community is different because it contains members of different species.

mcqs.q: Members of different species living together at a particular place are called a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is community. Members of different species living at one place together form a community, whereas a population has members of only one species.

mcqs.q: What do similar cells together make?
mcqs.why: Cells of the same kind together make a tissue. Tissues then join to form organs, so the tissue is the level that comes directly after the cell.

mcqs.q: What is the correct order of biological organisation?
mcqs.why: The order of organisation runs from small to large: atom, then molecule, then cell, then tissue, then organ. Every other option breaks this small-to-large sequence.

mcqs.q: Volvox is a multicellular body of which kind of algae?
mcqs.why: Volvox is a colony of green algae. It is the standard example of colonial organisation, in which many cells live together but each cell does its own work.

mcqs.q: What is the scientific name of the frog?
mcqs.why: The scientific name of the frog is Rana tigrina. This is a fixed scientific name given in the source, so the other names cannot be the correct answer.

mcqs.q: The part of the Earth where life is found is called the:
mcqs.why: The part of the Earth where life is found is the biosphere. It is the largest level of organisation, coming after population, community and ecosystem.

mcqs.q: Which set gives the six basic bio-elements correctly?
options: Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus and iron
Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus and sulphur
Carbon, oxygen, nitrogen, calcium, phosphorus and sulphur
Hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus, sulphur and zinc
mcqs.why: The six basic elements are carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus and sulphur. A list that leaves out sulphur is incomplete and therefore wrong.

mcqs.q: How is a species recognised?
options: When its members live at the same place
When its members look exactly alike
When its members can interbreed and produce fertile offspring
When its members live in water
mcqs.why: A species is recognised when its members can interbreed and produce fertile offspring. Living together at one place describes a population, not the test of a species.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between colonial and multicellular organisation?
options: There is no difference between them
In colonial organisation each cell does its own work, in multicellular organisation cells form tissues, organs and systems and work is divided
In colonial organisation cells form organs, in multicellular they do not
In multicellular organisation cells always live alone
mcqs.why: In colonial organisation, as in Volvox, many cells live together but each cell does its own work. In multicellular organisation cells form tissues, organs and systems and the work is divided.

lessons.title: 2.1 Biological Method
lessons.notes_html:
Biological Method — Introduction

Biologists face many questions about living things. The problems on which biologists do not agree, and on which scientists debate, are called biological problems. To solve such problems in a proper, scientific way, biologists use the biological method — the way of solving biological problems by the scientific method.

The biological method follows a fixed sequence of steps: problem → observation → hypothesis → reasoning → experiment → data collection → conclusion → theory → law. So, in short, the order runs from hypothesis to reasoning, then to theory, and finally to law.

StepEasy Meaning
ProblemThe biological problem to be solved — a problem on which scientists debate
ObservationLooking at something carefully and collecting information about it; the solution of a biological problem begins with observation
HypothesisA testable statement which is checked and confirmed through experiment
ReasoningThinking about the hypothesis — inductive reasoning and deductive reasoning
ExperimentThe practical test of the hypothesis
Data CollectionCollecting the results of the experiment; once data is in hand, its mathematical analysis is needed
ConclusionThe conclusion drawn from the experiment and the analysis of data
TheoryA tested explanation formed from tested conclusions
LawA statement of a uniform and constant natural fact, tested again and again

Biological Problems, Observation and Hypothesis

The solution of every biological problem begins with observation. Observation means looking at something carefully and collecting information about it.

  • Quantitative observation: In quantitative observation, instruments are used for numbers and measurement.

After observation comes the hypothesis. A hypothesis is a testable statement which is checked and confirmed — a statement that can be tested through experiment. The hypothesis is an important part of the scientific method.

An example from this unit: the cause of malaria is Plasmodium. A statement like this is first put forward as a hypothesis and is accepted only after it has been tested.

Reasoning — Inductive and Deductive

Reasoning is the step in which the hypothesis is thought through logically. There are two kinds of scientific reasoning:

  • Inductive reasoning: Reasoning from the specific to the general. In inductive reasoning, a general conclusion is drawn from specific observations.
  • Deductive reasoning: Reasoning based on "if-then" statements. In deductive reasoning, a specific conclusion is drawn from a general principle.
Inductive ReasoningDeductive Reasoning
A general conclusion is drawn from specific observationsA specific conclusion is drawn from a general principle
Moves from the specific to the generalUsually works with "if-then" statements

Experiment, Data Collection and Conclusion

An experiment is needed so that the hypothesis can be tested. Without experiment, a hypothesis cannot become a theory — this is why the experiment is such an essential step of the biological method.

During and after the experiment, data is collected. Once data is in hand, mathematical analysis of the data is needed. The conclusion drawn from the experiment and the analysis of data is called the derived conclusion.

Theory and Law

  • Theory: A theory is a tested explanation of a natural process. It is formed from tested conclusions. A theory is the most reliable scientific explanation because it has been tested again and again by experiments and it explains many observations.
  • Law: A law is a statement of a uniform and constant natural fact, which has been tested again and again. The unchanging answer to a uniform or constant natural fact is a law.
TheoryLaw
A tested explanation of a natural processA statement of a uniform and constant natural fact
A theory tells "why"A law tells "what happens"

Remember: theory, law and hypothesis are all parts of the biological method. Ratio is not — ratio is a concept of mathematics. In the same way, proportion is not a part of the biological method; the method includes problem, observation, hypothesis, experiment and data collection.

Organising Data — Tables, Graphs, Ratio and Proportion

Data must be arranged properly before it can be understood. Both tables and graphs are useful for arranging data — with them, data can be seen in order, compared, and patterns can be easily understood.

  • Graph: A graph is a way of showing data in picture form. The relationship between two variables is shown by means of a graph.
  • Ratio: Ratio is the comparison of two quantities, such as two divided by four.
  • Proportion: Proportion is an equation in which two ratios are equal. When two ratios are equal, that equation is a proportion.

Mathematics in Biology — Biomathematics and Mathematical Models

Mathematics plays an important role in solving biological problems. The science that studies biological systems by mathematical methods is called biomathematics.

A mathematical model is representing a biological system by mathematical equations and numbers. Biological science needs mathematical models so that data can be analysed, patterns can be understood and predictions can be made.

Remember: the biological method always moves in order — problem, observation, hypothesis, reasoning, experiment, data collection, conclusion, theory and law — and every hypothesis must pass the test of experiment before it can become a theory.

mcqs.q: What is the correct sequence of the biological method?
options: Problem → observation → hypothesis → reasoning → experiment → data collection → conclusion → theory → law
mcqs.why: The biological method runs in the order: problem, observation, hypothesis, reasoning, experiment, data collection, conclusion, theory and law. Every step must come in this sequence.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is the odd one out?
mcqs.why: Theory, law and hypothesis are all parts of the biological method, whereas ratio is a concept of mathematics. That is why ratio is the odd one out in this list.

mcqs.q: The science that studies biological systems by mathematical methods is called:
mcqs.why: In biomathematics, biological systems are studied by mathematical methods. The other names belong to different branches and do not mean the mathematical study of biological systems.

mcqs.q: The biological method includes all of the following EXCEPT:
mcqs.why: The biological method includes problem, observation, hypothesis, experiment and data collection. Proportion is not a part of the biological method, so it is the correct exception.

mcqs.q: Scientific reasoning from the specific to the general is called:
mcqs.why: In inductive reasoning a general conclusion is drawn from specific observations, so it moves from the specific to the general. Deductive reasoning moves the other way, from a general principle to a specific conclusion.

mcqs.q: What is used in quantitative observation?
mcqs.why: In quantitative observation, instruments are used for numbers and measurement. Quantitative observation deals with quantities, so measuring instruments are necessary for it.

mcqs.q: What is a hypothesis?
options: A testable statement which is checked and confirmed
A final conclusion of an experiment
A table used to arrange data
mcqs.why: A hypothesis is a statement that can be tested through experiment and is then checked and confirmed or rejected. It is not yet a law or a final conclusion when it is first proposed.

mcqs.q: How is the relationship between two variables shown?
mcqs.why: The relationship between two variables is shown by means of a graph. A graph shows data in picture form, which makes the relationship between the two variables clear.

mcqs.q: Which method is most useful for arranging data?
mcqs.why: Both tables and graphs are useful for arranging data. With them, data can be seen in order, compared, and patterns in the data can be easily understood.

mcqs.q: Problems on which biologists do not agree are called:
mcqs.why: Problems on which scientists debate and do not agree are called biological problems. The biological method is the scientific way used to solve exactly these problems.

mcqs.q: The solution of a biological problem begins with:
mcqs.why: The solution of a biological problem begins with observation — looking at something carefully and collecting information about it. All the later steps of the method come after this first step.

mcqs.q: Scientific reasoning based on "if-then" statements is called:
mcqs.why: Deductive reasoning is based on "if-then" statements and draws a specific conclusion from a general principle. Inductive reasoning is different: it draws a general conclusion from specific observations.

mcqs.q: The unchanging answer to a uniform or constant natural fact is a:
mcqs.why: A scientific law is a statement of a uniform and constant natural fact, tested again and again. A hypothesis is only a testable statement, and a theory is a tested explanation — neither is the unchanging statement itself.

mcqs.q: Why is a theory the most reliable scientific explanation?
options: Because it is the first guess of a scientist
Because it has been tested again and again by experiments and explains many observations
Because it is written as a mathematical equation
mcqs.why: A theory is the most reliable scientific explanation because it has been tested again and again by experiments and it explains many observations. A first guess is only a hypothesis, not a theory.

mcqs.q: The cause of malaria is:
mcqs.why: Malaria is caused by the organism called Plasmodium. This is the example used in this unit, while ratio, proportion and mathematical models are mathematical ideas, not causes of the disease.

lessons.title: 3.1 Introduction and Definition of Biodiversity
lessons.notes_html:
Introduction to Biodiversity

Biodiversity is about the differences found in living organisms. It does not mean the sameness among organisms, but the differences that exist between them.

Definition of Biodiversity

The differences present among species are called biodiversity.

  • A species is a distinct kind of organism, and different species differ from one another.
  • When we talk about these differences among species as a whole, we use the term biodiversity.
  • Biodiversity is therefore the name for variety and difference at the level of species.

Remember the definition in simple words: differences among species = biodiversity. This one definition is the base of this whole unit, because classification, the five kingdoms and conservation all start from the fact that species are different from one another.

mcqs.q: The differences present among species are called:
mcqs.why: The source answer states directly that the differences present among species are called biodiversity, not taxonomy or classification.

mcqs.q: What does the term biodiversity refer to?
options: The scientific name of a species
mcqs.why: Biodiversity refers to the differences present among species. The other options describe a name, a rank order and mycelium, which are different ideas.

mcqs.q: Differences are present among which of the following, according to the definition of biodiversity?
mcqs.why: The definition is built on species: the differences present among species are called biodiversity, so species is the correct level here.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly defines biodiversity?
options: It is the science of classification
It is a double scientific name
It is a rank larger than genus
It is the differences present among species
mcqs.why: The correct definition is the differences present among species. Taxonomy is the science of classification and a double name is binomial naming.

mcqs.q: If two species differ from each other, that difference is part of:
mcqs.why: Differences among species are called biodiversity, so any difference between species is part of biodiversity as defined in the source.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT the meaning of biodiversity?
mcqs.why: The science of classification is taxonomy, not biodiversity. Biodiversity means the differences present among species.

mcqs.q: Biodiversity is concerned with differences among:
mcqs.why: Biodiversity is concerned with species and the differences present among them, not with letters, cell walls or fungal threads.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct pair:
mcqs.why: Biodiversity is correctly paired with differences among species. A fungal thread is a hypha and a virus is the non-cellular parasite in the source.

mcqs.q: The word used for the differences present among species is:
mcqs.why: The source answer gives the word biodiversity for the differences present among species. Family, genus and species are ranks of classification.

mcqs.q: Why is the idea of 'difference among species' important in this unit?
options: Because it is the definition of biodiversity
Because it is the scientific name of the cat
Because it is the largest rank
mcqs.why: It is important because it is the very definition of biodiversity given in the source. The cat's name, hyphae and the largest rank are separate points.

lessons.title: 3.2 Principles and Aims of Classification
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Classification?

Classification is dividing organisms into groups on the basis of their characteristics.

The science of classification is called taxonomy.

Homologous and Analogous Structures

TypeMeaningRole in Classification
Homologous structuresStructures that have the same internal structure, even though their functions (physiology) are differentClassification is based on homologous structures
Analogous structuresStructures that do the same work but have different internal structureNot a basis for classification; in classification, all except analogous structures are involved

Taxonomic Hierarchy

Taxonomic hierarchy is the order of the ranks of classification. The correct order, from large to small, is:

Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species

RankMeaning from the Source
KingdomThe largest rank of classification, such as Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia
ClassA large rank; in a list with order, genus and species, class brings all the others into one circle because it is the largest among them
FamilyA rank smaller than order and larger than genus
GenusA rank smaller than family and larger than species; it includes closely related species
SpeciesThe group of organisms whose members can interbreed and produce fertile offspring

Purpose of Classification

  • To identify organisms.
  • To bring uniformity in their names.
  • To understand the relationships among organisms.

Classification is therefore not just making groups. Its hierarchy, from kingdom down to species, helps us identify each organism and understand how organisms are related to one another.

mcqs.q: Classification is:
options: Dividing organisms into groups on the basis of their characteristics
Giving every species a double name only
mcqs.why: Classification is dividing organisms into groups on the basis of their characteristics, as stated directly in the source definition.

mcqs.q: The science of classification is called:
mcqs.why: The science of classification is called taxonomy. Biodiversity is differences among species, and mycelium is the network of fungal hyphae.

mcqs.q: What is the correct order of classification?
options: Species → genus → family → order → class → phylum → kingdom
Kingdom → species → genus → family → order → class → phylum
Kingdom → phylum → class → order → family → genus → species
Phylum → kingdom → class → order → genus → family → species
mcqs.why: The order runs from large to small: kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species, exactly as given in the source answer.

mcqs.q: In classification, which one is NOT involved as a basis?
mcqs.why: Classification is based on homologous structures; analogous structures are the one exception that is not a basis for classification.

mcqs.q: Homologous structures have:
options: The same internal structure, though their functions may differ
Different internal structure and the same work
mcqs.why: Homologous structures have the same internal structure even though their functions are different, which is why classification is based on them.

mcqs.q: Analogous structures are structures that:
options: Do the same work but have different internal structure
Can interbreed and produce fertile offspring
mcqs.why: Analogous structures do the same work but have different internal structure, the opposite pattern to homologous structures in the source.

mcqs.q: A species is:
options: The group of organisms whose members can interbreed and produce fertile offspring
mcqs.why: A species is the group of organisms whose members can interbreed and produce fertile offspring, as defined in the source answers.

mcqs.q: Family is a rank that is:
options: Larger than kingdom and smaller than species
Smaller than genus and larger than species
Larger than order and smaller than kingdom
Smaller than order and larger than genus
mcqs.why: Family is smaller than order and larger than genus, which places it between order and genus in the taxonomic hierarchy.

mcqs.q: Genus is a rank that is:
options: Smaller than family and larger than species, including closely related species
mcqs.why: Genus is smaller than family and larger than species, and it includes closely related species, according to the source definition.

mcqs.q: The purpose of classification is to:
options: Identify organisms, bring uniformity in their names, and understand relationships among them
mcqs.why: The stated purpose is to identify organisms, bring uniformity in their names and understand the relationships among them.

lessons.title: 3.3 History of Classification
lessons.notes_html:
Classification into Three Kingdoms

One stage in the history of classification grouped organisms into three kingdoms. The chart of three kingdoms in the source is:

KingdomWhat It Contains
ProtistaUnicellular eukaryotic organisms
PlantaePlants
AnimaliaAnimals

The Four-Kingdom Stage and Kingdom Metaphyta

Classification later used four kingdoms. In the four-kingdom classification, Kingdom Metaphyta is the plant kingdom.

  • Metaphyta includes bryophyta.
  • Metaphyta includes gymnosperms.
  • Metaphyta includes angiosperms.
  • Metaphyta does not include algae.

So, in the history of classification, the number of kingdoms grew, and the groups placed inside each kingdom also changed. The key test point from this stage is simple: algae are the exception — they are not included in Kingdom Metaphyta, while bryophyta, gymnosperms and angiosperms are.

mcqs.q: In the four-kingdom classification, Kingdom Metaphyta includes all of the following EXCEPT:
mcqs.why: Kingdom Metaphyta includes bryophyta, gymnosperms and angiosperms; algae are not included in it, so algae is the exception.

mcqs.q: Which group IS included in Kingdom Metaphyta?
mcqs.why: Bryophyta is included in Metaphyta, the plant kingdom. Algae is the stated exception, and Amoeba belongs to Protista in the source.

mcqs.q: In the chart of three kingdoms, Protista contains:
mcqs.why: The three-kingdom chart describes Protista as unicellular eukaryotic organisms, Plantae as plants and Animalia as animals.

mcqs.q: In the chart of three kingdoms, Plantae contains:
mcqs.why: In the three-kingdom chart, Plantae stands for plants, Animalia for animals and Protista for unicellular eukaryotic organisms.

mcqs.q: In the chart of three kingdoms, Animalia contains:
mcqs.why: Animalia in the three-kingdom chart contains animals. The other two kingdoms in the chart are Protista and Plantae.

mcqs.q: How many kingdoms are shown in the three-kingdom chart?
mcqs.why: The chart shows three kingdoms: Protista, Plantae and Animalia, which is why it is called the classification of three kingdoms.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a member of the three-kingdom chart?
mcqs.why: Protista is one of the three kingdoms in the chart, together with Plantae and Animalia, as given in the source answer.

mcqs.q: Kingdom Metaphyta belongs to which stage of classification?
mcqs.why: The source question places Kingdom Metaphyta in the four-kingdom classification, where it includes bryophyta, gymnosperms and angiosperms.

mcqs.q: Which pair is correctly matched with Metaphyta?
mcqs.why: Gymnosperms are included in Metaphyta. Algae are explicitly not included, and Amoeba and viruses are not placed in Metaphyta.

mcqs.q: Which group is the odd one out for Kingdom Metaphyta?
mcqs.why: Algae is the odd one out because Metaphyta includes bryophyta, gymnosperms and angiosperms, but does not include algae.

lessons.title: 3.4 The Five Kingdoms
lessons.notes_html:
How the Five Kingdoms Were Made

Organisms were classified into five kingdoms on the basis of their cell structure, method of obtaining food and body structure: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.

KingdomMain FeaturesExample / Note
MoneraProkaryotic, unicellular; no true nucleusBacteria; cyanobacteria are placed here because they are prokaryotic
ProtistaEukaryotic, mostly unicellular; has a true nucleus; many protists are unicellularAmoeba
FungiEukaryotic, heterotrophic, no chlorophyll, food taken by absorption; cell wall made of chitinMushroom
PlantaeEukaryotic, autotrophic, has chlorophyll; cell wall made of cellulosePlants
AnimaliaEukaryotic, heterotrophic, multicellularAnimals; multicellular animals are also called Metazoa

Important Differences

ComparisonFirst GroupSecond Group
Monera vs ProtistaMonera: prokaryotic, no true nucleusProtista: eukaryotic, has a true nucleus
Fungi vs PlantaeFungi: no chlorophyll, heterotrophic, chitin wallPlantae: chlorophyll present, autotrophic, cellulose wall
Plantae vs AnimaliaPlantae: make their own food (autotrophic), cells contain chlorophyllAnimalia: depend on others for food (heterotrophic), no chlorophyll

Fungi: Hyphae and Mycelium

  • Hyphae are the thin threads of fungi.
  • Mycelium is the network of hyphae (threads) of fungi.
  • Fungi have no chlorophyll and take food by absorption, so organisms without chlorophyll that absorb food are fungi.

Why Amoeba Is Not in Animalia

Amoeba is not a member of the animal kingdom but of Protista. It has not been placed in the animal kingdom because it is unicellular and has no tissues and organs. So the pair Animalia → Amoeba is wrongly matched.

Where Are Viruses Placed?

Viruses are not placed in any of the five kingdoms. A virus is a non-cellular parasite, and it has not been placed in any kingdom because it is not cellular; it is neither living nor dead, but in between the two.

mcqs.q: Members of which kingdom are all heterotrophic and have a chitin cell wall?
mcqs.why: Members of Fungi are all heterotrophic and their cell wall is made of chitin, as stated directly in the source answer.

mcqs.q: In the five-kingdom system, where are viruses placed?
options: In none of the five kingdoms
mcqs.why: Viruses are not placed in any of the five kingdoms because they are not cellular, so the correct choice is none of these kingdoms.

mcqs.q: Choose the wrongly matched pair:
mcqs.why: Animalia to Amoeba is wrongly matched because Amoeba is a member of Protista, not of the animal kingdom.

mcqs.q: Many protists are:
mcqs.why: Many protists are unicellular organisms, and Protista are eukaryotic, which separates them from prokaryotic Monera.

mcqs.q: Organisms without chlorophyll that take food by absorption are:
mcqs.why: Fungi have no chlorophyll and they take food by absorption, which is the defining feeding method given for fungi in the source.

mcqs.q: The main difference between Monera and Protista is:
options: Monera have chlorophyll, Protista do not
Monera are prokaryotic with no true nucleus, Protista are eukaryotic with a true nucleus
Monera are multicellular, Protista are not
mcqs.why: Monera are prokaryotic, meaning no true nucleus, while Protista are eukaryotic, meaning they have a true nucleus.

mcqs.q: Fungi differ from Plantae because fungi:
options: Have no chlorophyll, are heterotrophic and have a chitin wall
mcqs.why: Fungi have no chlorophyll, are heterotrophic and have a chitin wall, while Plantae have chlorophyll, are autotrophic and have a cellulose wall.

mcqs.q: Mycelium is:
options: The scientific name of the cat
The network of hyphae of fungi
mcqs.why: Mycelium is the network of hyphae, the thin threads of fungi, which together form the fungal body described in the source.

mcqs.q: Hyphae are:
options: The thin threads of fungi which together make mycelium
Structures with the same internal structure
The two parts of a scientific name
mcqs.why: Hyphae are the thin threads of fungi, and together they make the mycelium, as defined in the source answers.

mcqs.q: Why has the virus not been placed in any kingdom?
options: Because it is not cellular; it is neither living nor dead, but in between
mcqs.why: The virus is not cellular and is described as neither living nor dead but in between, so it is placed in none of the kingdoms.

lessons.title: 3.5 Binomial Nomenclature
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Binomial Nomenclature?

Every species is given a double (binomial) scientific name. A scientific name is written by the binomial method:

  • The first name is of the genus.
  • The second name is of the species.

How a Scientific Name Is Written

Rule / PartDetail
Number of namesDouble — genus name + species name
LettersWritten in slanting (italic) letters
DogCanis lupus
CatFelis catus — the biological name of the cat

Why Is a Scientific Name Necessary?

A scientific name is necessary so that the same organism is known by the same name everywhere in the world and there is no confusion.

The correct way to write the scientific name of an organism is the binomial way, as in Canis lupus for the dog: genus first, species second, in slanting (italic) letters.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct way to write the scientific name of the dog?
mcqs.why: Canis lupus is correct because a scientific name is written by the binomial method, genus first and species second; it is the dog's name.

mcqs.q: The biological name of the cat is:
mcqs.why: The scientific name of the cat is Felis catus. Canis lupus is the scientific name of the dog given in the source.

mcqs.q: A species is given which kind of scientific name?
mcqs.why: Every species is given a double scientific name: the name of the genus and the name of the species, which is the binomial method.

mcqs.q: A scientific name is written in which letters?
mcqs.why: A scientific name is written in slanting, that is italic, letters, as stated directly in the source fill-in answer.

mcqs.q: In a binomial name, the first and second names are of:
mcqs.why: In the binomial method the first name is of the genus and the second is of the species, as shown in Canis lupus.

mcqs.q: Why is a scientific name necessary?
options: So the same organism is known by the same name everywhere and there is no confusion
mcqs.why: A scientific name is necessary so the same organism is known by the same name everywhere in the world and there is no confusion.

mcqs.q: Which statement about binomial naming is correct?
options: The name has two parts: genus and species
The name is never written in italic
mcqs.why: A binomial name has two parts, genus first and species second, and it is written in slanting italic letters.

mcqs.q: Canis lupus is the scientific name of:
mcqs.why: Canis lupus is the scientific name of the dog. The cat is Felis catus, which is the other example given in the source.

mcqs.q: Felis catus tells us that Felis is the:
mcqs.why: In a binomial name the first name is the genus, so in Felis catus, Felis is the genus and catus is the species.

mcqs.q: If an organism is known by different names in different places, the problem is solved by:
options: A single scientific name used everywhere
mcqs.why: A scientific name solves confusion because the same organism is known by the same name everywhere in the world.

lessons.title: 3.6 Conservation of Biodiversity
lessons.notes_html:
What Affects Biodiversity?

Biodiversity is affected by all three of these:

  • Deforestation
  • Environmental damage
  • Illegal hunting

Effect of Deforestation on Biodiversity

Deforestation destroys the homes of organisms, reduces the number of species, and many species fall into danger. That is why biodiversity decreases.

  • Homes of organisms are destroyed.
  • The number of species is reduced.
  • Many species fall into danger.
  • Result: biodiversity decreases.

Endangered Species

An endangered species is a species which faces the danger of permanent extinction. Animals which face the danger of permanent extinction are called endangered species.

Conservation of biodiversity therefore means protecting species from these dangers — deforestation, environmental damage and illegal hunting — so that species do not become endangered and biodiversity does not keep decreasing.

mcqs.q: What affects biodiversity?
options: Deforestation, environmental damage and illegal hunting — all three
mcqs.why: Biodiversity is affected by deforestation, environmental damage and illegal hunting, all three together, as stated in the source answer.

mcqs.q: Animals which face the danger of permanent extinction are called:
mcqs.why: Such animals are called endangered species because an endangered species faces the danger of permanent extinction.

mcqs.q: Deforestation affects biodiversity because it:
options: Destroys the homes of organisms and reduces the number of species
mcqs.why: Deforestation destroys the homes of organisms, reduces the number of species and puts many species in danger, so biodiversity decreases.

mcqs.q: An endangered species is a species which:
options: Faces the danger of permanent extinction
mcqs.why: An endangered species faces the danger of permanent extinction, which is the exact definition given in the source answers.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is listed as affecting biodiversity?
mcqs.why: Deforestation is one of the three factors listed: deforestation, environmental damage and illegal hunting all affect biodiversity.

mcqs.q: Illegal hunting is harmful because, according to the source, it is:
options: One of the factors that affect biodiversity
mcqs.why: Illegal hunting is listed with deforestation and environmental damage as a factor that affects biodiversity.

mcqs.q: After deforestation, what happens to many species?
mcqs.why: Deforestation reduces the number of species and many species fall into danger, which is why biodiversity decreases.

mcqs.q: The final result of deforestation described in the source is:
mcqs.why: Because homes are destroyed and species are reduced and put in danger, the result stated in the source is that biodiversity decreases.

mcqs.q: Environmental damage is grouped in the source with:
options: Deforestation and illegal hunting as factors affecting biodiversity
Genus and species as parts of a name
Hyphae and mycelium as fungal parts
Kingdom and phylum as ranks only
mcqs.why: Environmental damage is grouped with deforestation and illegal hunting; all three are the factors that affect biodiversity.

mcqs.q: A species in danger of permanent extinction needs conservation because it is:
mcqs.why: A species facing permanent extinction is an endangered species, and such species are at the centre of conservation of biodiversity.

lessons.title: Microscopic Structure of the Cell
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Microscope?

A microscope is the instrument with which small things can be seen magnified. In a microscope the visible image is magnified, so very small structures such as cells can be studied.

Magnification

Magnification is making the image of an object larger than the original in a microscope. In a light microscope the combination of the eyepiece lens and the objective lens gives a magnification of about 1000 times.

Resolution

Resolution is the smallest distance between two close points in a microscope that can still be seen separately. The smallest distance between two points is called resolution.

Light Microscope and Electron Microscope

A microscope has two main types. The light microscope uses light and its magnification is about 1000 times. The electron microscope uses an electron beam and its resolution and magnification are much greater.

  • In the electron microscope the wavelength of the electron beam is short, so its resolution is greater.
  • Ordinary light has a longer wavelength than electrons, so the electron microscope gives clearer images than an ordinary microscope.
  • The short wavelength of the electron beam is responsible for the greater resolution of the electron microscope.
FeatureLight (Simple Compound) MicroscopeElectron Microscope
Beam usedLightElectron beam
MagnificationAbout 1000 timesMuch greater
ResolutionLessMuch greater, because the electron beam has a short wavelength
ImagesLess clearClearer images

In short, the electron microscope is different from the simple compound microscope because it uses an electron beam instead of light, and its resolution and magnification are much greater.

mcqs.q: What is responsible for the greater resolution of the electron microscope?
options: The short wavelength of the electron beam
The large size of the specimen
mcqs.why: The short wavelength of the electron beam gives the electron microscope its greater resolution, because a shorter wavelength can separate two very close points more clearly.

mcqs.q: In a microscope, the visible image is:
mcqs.why: In a microscope the visible image is magnified. Magnifying the image is the main job of a microscope, so small objects can be seen in detail.

mcqs.q: In microscopy, the smallest distance between two points is called:
mcqs.why: The smallest distance between two points is called resolution. It tells how close two points can be while still being seen as separate points.

mcqs.q: The magnification of a light microscope, with the combination of lenses, is about:
mcqs.why: In a light microscope the combination of the eyepiece lens and the objective lens gives a magnification of about 1000 times.

mcqs.q: Ordinary light has a longer wavelength than electrons, so the electron microscope gives ______ images.
mcqs.why: The electron microscope gives clearer images than an ordinary microscope because ordinary light has a longer wavelength than electrons, and the short electron wavelength gives better resolution.

mcqs.q: What is magnification?
options: The movement of substances through a membrane
Making the image of an object larger than the original in a microscope
A group of cells doing one job
mcqs.why: Magnification is making the image of an object larger than the original in a microscope. It is different from resolution, which is about separating two close points.

mcqs.q: What is resolution?
options: Making an image larger than the original
The flattened sacs of the endoplasmic reticulum
The smallest distance between two close points that can still be seen separately
mcqs.why: Resolution is the smallest distance between two close points in a microscope that can still be seen separately. Greater resolution means a clearer and more detailed image.

mcqs.q: How is the electron microscope different from the simple compound microscope?
options: It uses an electron beam and its resolution and magnification are much greater
It uses light and magnifies about 1000 times only
It does not magnify the image at all
It is used without any beam
mcqs.why: In the electron microscope an electron beam is used and its resolution and magnification are much greater, while the simple compound microscope uses light and magnifies about 1000 times.

mcqs.q: What is a microscope?
options: A small sac that carries substances in the cell
An instrument with which small things can be seen magnified
A group of cells of the same kind
The control centre of the cell
mcqs.why: A microscope is the instrument with which small things can be seen magnified. Its two main types are the light microscope and the electron microscope.

mcqs.q: Which microscope uses an electron beam instead of light?
mcqs.why: The electron microscope uses an electron beam instead of light. Because the electron beam has a short wavelength, its resolution and magnification are much greater.

lessons.title: History of the Cell Theory
lessons.notes_html:
Cell Theory

The postulates of cell theory are: all living things are made of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and new cells arise from pre-existing cells. The statement that the material of the cell membrane has no hereditary material is not a postulate of cell theory.

The nucleus inside the cell holds hereditary information and controls all the activities of the cell.

Prokaryotic and Eukaryotic Cells

FeatureProkaryotic CellEukaryotic Cell
True nucleusNo true nucleusHas a true nucleus
Membrane-bound organellesNo membrane-bound organellesHas membrane-bound organelles

Cell Wall

In plants, the strong fibres of the cell wall are made of cellulose. The secondary cell wall is made of cellulose and lignin.

Cell Membrane and the Fluid Mosaic Model

The cell membrane is made of a phospholipid bilayer and proteins. According to the fluid mosaic model, the cell membrane is made of a phospholipid bilayer in which pieces of protein float, like things floating in water. Proteins and carbohydrates can change place in the membrane, so the membrane is flexible and moving.

The cell membrane is semi-permeable because some substances can pass through it and some cannot, which keeps the inside of the cell controlled.

Nucleus

The nucleus is the control centre of the cell. Around it is a double membrane with pores. Inside are nucleoplasm, nucleolus and chromosomes. Nucleoplasm is the fluid inside the nucleus in which chromosomes and the nucleolus are present. The nucleus controls all the activities of the cell and holds hereditary information.

Endoplasmic Reticulum, Ribosomes and Golgi Body

  • The rough endoplasmic reticulum makes proteins, and the smooth endoplasmic reticulum makes lipids and steroids.
  • Ribosomes make proteins, not steroids; steroids are made in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
  • Cisternae are the flattened sacs of the endoplasmic reticulum and the Golgi body.
  • The correct sequence for a protein is: Ribosome, then endoplasmic reticulum, then Golgi body, then lysosome. A protein is made in the ribosome, then goes from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi body and then to the lysosome.
  • Vesicles are small sacs in the cell in which substances are enclosed and carried from one place to another.

Cell Organelles: Lysosomes, Mitochondria and Chloroplasts

OrganelleMain WorkWhere Found / Note
LysosomeContains digestive enzymes which help in digestion inside the cell and break things downSmall organelles of animal cells that help in intracellular digestion
RibosomeMakes proteinsDoes not make steroids
MitochondrionProduces energy in the form of ATP through respiration; called the powerhouse of the cellPresent in all eukaryotic cells
ChloroplastMakes food with light energy by photosynthesisPresent only in plant cells

The mitochondrion is called the powerhouse of the cell because in it energy is produced in the form of ATP through respiration.

Centrioles

The microscopic tubules arranged in a special pattern to form centrioles are 27 in number, that is 9 groups of three.

Movement Into and Out of the Cell

Osmosis, diffusion and active transport all three cause the movement of substances into and out of the cell.

  • Diffusion is a passive process in which no energy is spent.
  • Diffusion, facilitated diffusion and osmosis are passive processes in which no energy is spent; active transport uses energy, so active transport is the odd one out among them.
  • Facilitated diffusion is a special type of diffusion of specific substances through carrier proteins. In facilitated diffusion substances move from higher to lower concentration through carrier proteins and no energy is spent.
  • In active transport substances move from lower to higher concentration and energy is spent.
  • Exocytosis is the process in which things from inside the cell are pushed out of the cell by means of vesicles.
  • When a plant cell loses water, the cytoplasm shrinks, and this process is called plasmolysis.
ProcessDirectionEnergySpecial Point
Facilitated diffusionHigher to lower concentrationNo energy spentThrough carrier proteins
Active transportLower to higher concentrationEnergy spentUses energy, unlike passive processes

mcqs.q: In cell theory, all except one are postulates. Which is the one that is NOT a postulate?
options: All living things are made of cells
The cell is the basic unit of life
The material of the cell membrane has no hereditary material
New cells arise from pre-existing cells
mcqs.why: The postulates of cell theory are that all living things are made of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and new cells arise from pre-existing cells, so the membrane statement is not a postulate.

mcqs.q: What are the functions of the endoplasmic reticulum?
options: Synthesis of proteins, and lipids and steroids
mcqs.why: The rough endoplasmic reticulum makes proteins, and the smooth endoplasmic reticulum makes lipids and steroids, so synthesis of proteins is its key function among the choices.

mcqs.q: Which processes drive the movement of things into and out of the cell?
options: Osmosis, diffusion and active transport together
mcqs.why: Osmosis, diffusion and active transport all three cause the movement of substances into and out of the cell, so all three processes together are correct.

mcqs.q: What is the secondary cell wall made of?
mcqs.why: The secondary cell wall is made of cellulose and lignin. Cellulose also makes the strong fibres of the plant cell wall, and lignin is added in the secondary wall.

mcqs.q: Choose the odd one out: diffusion, facilitated diffusion, osmosis and active transport.
mcqs.why: Diffusion, facilitated diffusion and osmosis are passive processes in which no energy is spent, while active transport uses energy, so active transport is the odd one out.

mcqs.q: What is the correct sequence for a protein to reach the Golgi body?
options: Golgi body, then ribosome, then lysosome
Ribosome, then endoplasmic reticulum, then Golgi body, then lysosome
Lysosome, then ribosome, then Golgi body
Endoplasmic reticulum, then lysosome, then ribosome
mcqs.why: A protein is made in the ribosome, then goes from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi body and then to the lysosome, so that is the correct sequence.

mcqs.q: Which small organelles from animal cells help in intracellular digestion?
mcqs.why: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes which help in digestion inside the cell, so lysosomes are the organelles that help in intracellular digestion.

mcqs.q: Choose the mismatched pair.
options: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum and synthesis of steroids
mcqs.why: Ribosomes make proteins, not steroids; steroids are made in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum, so ribosome with synthesis of steroids is the mismatched pair.

mcqs.q: In plants, the strong fibres of the cell wall are made of:
mcqs.why: The strong fibres of the plant cell wall are made of cellulose. The secondary cell wall is also made of cellulose together with lignin.

mcqs.q: The cell membrane is made of:
mcqs.why: The cell membrane is made of a phospholipid bilayer and proteins. In the fluid mosaic model, pieces of protein float in this bilayer.

mcqs.q: When a plant cell loses water, the cytoplasm ______ and this process is called ______.
mcqs.why: When a plant cell loses water, the cytoplasm shrinks; this process is called plasmolysis. It is the shrinking of cytoplasm due to water loss.

mcqs.q: A special type of diffusion of specific substances through carrier proteins is called:
mcqs.why: The movement of specific substances through carrier proteins is called facilitated diffusion. It moves substances from higher to lower concentration without spending energy.

mcqs.q: The microscopic tubules arranged in a special pattern to form centrioles are ______ in number.
mcqs.why: A centriole has 27 microscopic tubules, arranged as 9 groups of three. The number 9 alone counts only the groups, not the total tubules.

mcqs.q: What is the basic difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: A prokaryotic cell has no true nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles, while a eukaryotic cell has both
A eukaryotic cell has no nucleus
mcqs.why: A prokaryotic cell has no true nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles, while a eukaryotic cell has a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

mcqs.q: Why is the mitochondrion called the powerhouse of the cell?
options: Because it makes food by photosynthesis
Because energy is produced in it in the form of ATP through respiration
mcqs.why: The mitochondrion is called the powerhouse of the cell because in it energy is produced in the form of ATP through respiration, which powers the activities of the cell.

lessons.title: Cell Size and Shape in Relation to Surface Area and Volume
lessons.notes_html:
The Cell as the Structural and Functional Unit

The cell of organisms is called the structural and functional unit. It is called structural because all organisms are made of cells, and it is called functional because all the activities of life take place in the cell itself.

Activity: Looking at Plant Cells Under the Microscope

Onion peel is used to observe plant cells under the microscope. Iodine is used for onion peel because iodine stains the nucleus and other parts, so they can be seen clearly in the microscope.

  • Iodine stains the nucleus and other parts of the cell.
  • Because of this staining, the parts can be seen clearly in the microscope.

Note: This lesson is short in the English source pairs. Only the onion-peel activity and the idea of the cell as the structural and functional unit are given in the source for this topic, so no extra facts about cell sizes or surface area and volume have been added here.

mcqs.q: Why is iodine used for onion peel?
options: To produce energy in the cell
To stain the nucleus and other parts so they can be seen clearly in the microscope
To make the cell wall dissolve
mcqs.why: Iodine is used for onion peel because iodine stains the nucleus and other parts, so they can be seen clearly in the microscope during observation.

mcqs.q: What does iodine stain in the onion peel cell?
mcqs.why: Iodine stains the nucleus and other parts of the onion peel cell. This staining is what makes those parts visible clearly in the microscope.

mcqs.q: After staining with iodine, the nucleus and other parts can be:
mcqs.why: After iodine staining, the nucleus and other parts can be seen clearly in the microscope, which is the whole purpose of using iodine for onion peel.

mcqs.q: Why is the cell called the structural unit of organisms?
options: Because all organisms are made of cells
Because it is made of cellulose
mcqs.why: The cell is called the structural unit because all organisms are made of cells. Their bodies are built from cells, so the cell is the building unit.

mcqs.q: Why is the cell called the functional unit of organisms?
options: Because it is seen with iodine only
Because it has a secondary cell wall
Because all the activities of life take place in the cell itself
mcqs.why: The cell is called the functional unit because all the activities of life take place in the cell itself, not outside it.

mcqs.q: The cell is called the structural and functional unit because:
options: It has a true nucleus only
All organisms are made of cells and all activities of life take place in the cell itself
It gives clearer images than a microscope
It is made of a phospholipid bilayer
mcqs.why: The cell is the structural and functional unit because all organisms are made of cells and all the activities of life take place in the cell itself, covering both reasons together.

mcqs.q: Which part is specially mentioned as stained by iodine in onion peel?
mcqs.why: The nucleus is specially mentioned as stained by iodine, along with other parts, so that it can be seen clearly in the microscope.

mcqs.q: Onion peel cells are observed clearly with the help of:
mcqs.why: Onion peel is observed with iodine staining and a microscope: iodine stains the nucleus and other parts so they can be seen clearly in the microscope.

mcqs.q: Which statement about iodine and onion peel is correct?
options: Iodine produces ATP in onion cells
Iodine stains parts so they can be seen clearly
Iodine forms the secondary cell wall
mcqs.why: Iodine stains the nucleus and other parts so they can be seen clearly in the microscope. It does not produce energy or make proteins in this activity.

mcqs.q: All the activities of life take place in:
options: The onion peel only as food
mcqs.why: All the activities of life take place in the cell itself, which is why the cell is called the functional unit as well as the structural unit.

lessons.title: Animal and Plant Tissues
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Tissue?

A tissue is a group of cells of the same kind which together do a particular job.

  • A tissue is a group, not a single cell.
  • The cells in a tissue are of the same kind.
  • Together, these cells do a particular job.

In other words, cells of the same kind join together and work together for one particular job, and this group is called a tissue. Animal and plant bodies are built from such groups of cells working together.

Note: This lesson is short in the English source pairs. Only the definition of a tissue is given in the source for this topic, so no extra lists of tissue types have been added here.

mcqs.q: What is a tissue?
options: A single cell doing all jobs alone
A group of cells of the same kind which together do a particular job
A small sac that carries substances
mcqs.why: A tissue is a group of cells of the same kind which together do a particular job. It must be a group, the cells must be of the same kind, and they work together.

mcqs.q: The cells in a tissue are:
options: All of different kinds with no common job
mcqs.why: The cells in a tissue are of the same kind. A group of cells of the same kind doing a particular job together is the definition of a tissue.

mcqs.q: What do the cells of a tissue do together?
options: They do a particular job together
mcqs.why: The cells of a tissue together do a particular job. Working together for one particular job is part of the definition of a tissue.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is necessary for a group to be called a tissue?
options: Cells of the same kind working together for a particular job
mcqs.why: For a group to be called a tissue, it must be cells of the same kind which together do a particular job, as given in the definition of tissue.

mcqs.q: A tissue is best described as a ______ of cells.
mcqs.why: A tissue is a group of cells, not a single cell. That group consists of cells of the same kind which together do a particular job.

mcqs.q: Which statement is correct about a tissue?
options: It is the smallest distance between two points
It is made in the ribosome
It is a group of same-kind cells doing a particular job together
mcqs.why: A tissue is a group of cells of the same kind which together do a particular job. The other statements describe resolution, ribosomes or lysosomes, not a tissue.

mcqs.q: If cells are of the same kind and together do a particular job, they form a:
mcqs.why: Cells of the same kind which together do a particular job form a tissue. Vesicles, centrioles and cisternae are parts inside a cell, not groups of cells.

mcqs.q: The word 'together' in the definition of tissue shows that its cells:
options: Work together for a particular job
Can be seen without a microscope
mcqs.why: The cells of a tissue work together to do a particular job. A tissue is therefore a working group of same-kind cells, not separate unrelated cells.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT a tissue?
options: A group of same-kind cells doing a particular job together
A group of cells of the same kind working together
Cells of the same kind joined for one job
A single organelle inside one cell
mcqs.why: A single organelle inside one cell is not a tissue, because a tissue is a group of cells of the same kind which together do a particular job.

mcqs.q: A particular job done together by same-kind cells is done by a:
mcqs.why: A particular job done together by cells of the same kind is done by a tissue, which is defined as a group of such cells working together.

lessons.title: Chromosomes
lessons.notes_html:
What Are Chromosomes?

Chromosomes are thread-like structures. They appear in the cell at the time of cell division.

Parts of a Chromosome

A chromosome consists of two halves called chromatids. The two chromatids are joined to each other at a point called the centromere.

  • Chromatids: the two halves of a chromosome, joined at the centromere.
  • Centromere: the point (part) of the chromosome where the two chromatids are joined to each other.

Sister Chromatids and Homologous Chromosomes

  • Two chromatids that are genetically identical and copies of each other are called sister chromatids.
  • Chromosomes in a cell that are similar in arrangement to each other are called homologous chromosomes.

Key Terms

TermMeaning
ChromosomeThread-like structure that appears at the time of cell division
ChromatidsThe two halves of a chromosome joined at the centromere
CentromereThe point where two chromatids are joined
Sister chromatidsTwo chromatids that are genetically identical copies of each other
Homologous chromosomesChromosomes similar in arrangement to each other
Acrocentric chromosomeA chromosome in which one arm is very short and the other arm is very long

mcqs.q: Chromosomes are thread-like structures that appear at the time of .........
mcqs.why: Chromosomes appear at the time of cell division. The rest of the time the hereditary material stays spread out in the nucleus and is not seen as separate thread-like chromosomes.

mcqs.q: The point where two chromatids are joined is called the .........
mcqs.why: The two chromatids of a chromosome are joined at the centromere. It is the joining point of the chromosome, not a gene or the nucleolus.

mcqs.q: Chromatids are .........
options: the two halves of a chromosome joined at the centromere
mcqs.why: A chromatid is one of the two halves of a chromosome, and the two halves stay joined at the centromere until they separate during division.

mcqs.q: Two chromatids that are genetically identical and copies of each other are called .........
mcqs.why: Genetically identical copies joined in one chromosome are sister chromatids. Homologous chromosomes are similar in arrangement but are not identical copies of each other.

mcqs.q: Chromosomes in a cell that are similar in arrangement to each other are called .........
mcqs.why: Chromosomes that match each other in arrangement form a homologous pair. Sister chromatids, by contrast, are the two identical halves of a single chromosome.

mcqs.q: A chromosome in which one arm is very short and the other arm is very long is called .........
mcqs.why: In an acrocentric chromosome the centromere sits so that one arm is very short and the other arm is very long, unlike a metacentric chromosome with equal arms.

mcqs.q: Which part of the chromosome joins the two chromatids together?
mcqs.why: The centromere is the part of the chromosome where the two chromatids are joined to each other; the arms are the parts on either side of it.

mcqs.q: Which statement about chromosomes is correct?
options: They are visible all the time in the nucleus
They are thread-like and appear at cell division
They are found only in gametes
mcqs.why: Chromosomes are thread-like structures that appear at the time of cell division. They are present in dividing body cells as well, not only in gametes.

mcqs.q: Sister chromatids are best described as .........
options: genetically identical copies of each other
mcqs.why: Sister chromatids are two chromatids that are genetically identical and copies of each other, formed from the same chromosome.

mcqs.q: Homologous chromosomes are .........
options: the two halves of one chromosome
similar in arrangement to each other
mcqs.why: Homologous chromosomes are separate chromosomes that are similar in arrangement to each other. The two halves of one chromosome are chromatids, not homologues.

lessons.title: The Cell Cycle
lessons.notes_html:
What Is the Cell Cycle?

The series of changes between one cell division and the next is called the cell cycle. It is the full sequence a cell passes through from one division to the next division.

Interphase — the Growth Stage

Interphase is the stage in which the cell grows and enzymes are made. It is called the growth process because during it:

  • The cell grows in size.
  • Enzymes are made.
  • DNA is copied.
  • Preparation for division takes place.

Cytokinesis — Division of the Cytoplasm

Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm of the cell. By cytokinesis the cell finally divides into two parts, completing one turn of the cell cycle.

TermMeaning
Cell cycleThe series of changes between one cell division and the next
InterphaseThe stage in which the cell grows and enzymes are made; DNA is copied and the cell prepares for division
CytokinesisThe division of the cytoplasm of the cell

mcqs.q: The series of changes between one cell division and the next is called the .........
mcqs.why: The cell cycle is the series of changes from one cell division to the next. It covers the growth of the cell, the copying of DNA and the division itself.

mcqs.q: The stage in which the cell grows and enzymes are made is called .........
mcqs.why: During interphase the cell grows and enzymes are made. Metaphase, anaphase and telophase are stages of the division itself, not of growth.

mcqs.q: Why is interphase called the growth process?
options: Because the chromosomes line up at the equator
Because the cell divides into two in it
Because chromatids move to the poles in it
Because in it the cell grows, DNA is copied and preparation for division takes place
mcqs.why: Interphase is the growth process because in it the cell grows, DNA is copied and preparation for division takes place, before the actual division begins.

mcqs.q: Cytokinesis is .........
options: the division of the cytoplasm of the cell
mcqs.why: Cytokinesis means the division of the cytoplasm. The division of the nucleus is a different part of cell division, and DNA copying happens in interphase.

mcqs.q: Which of the following happens during interphase?
options: Chromosomes line up at the equator
The cell grows and DNA is copied
mcqs.why: In interphase the cell grows, enzymes are made and DNA is copied. Lining up at the equator and reaching the poles are events of the division stages, and cytoplasm division is cytokinesis.

mcqs.q: The cell cycle runs from .........
options: one cell division to the next
birth of the organism to its death
one gamete to the next gamete
mcqs.why: The cell cycle is defined for a single cell: it is the series of changes between one cell division and the next division of that cell.

mcqs.q: DNA is copied during .........
mcqs.why: DNA is copied in interphase, the growth stage in which the cell also grows and prepares for division. By metaphase the chromosomes are already duplicated.

mcqs.q: Which sequence is correct for a dividing cell?
options: Interphase (growth and DNA copying), then division, then cytokinesis
Division first, then DNA is copied
mcqs.why: The cell first passes through interphase, where it grows and copies its DNA, then divides, and cytokinesis divides the cytoplasm to complete the cycle.

mcqs.q: Enzymes needed by the cell are made mainly in .........
mcqs.why: Interphase is the stage in which the cell grows and enzymes are made, as the cell prepares itself for the coming division.

mcqs.q: Cytokinesis completes the cell cycle by .........
options: dividing the cytoplasm so the cell splits into two parts
mcqs.why: Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm of the cell, so the cell divides into two parts and one full turn of the cell cycle is completed.

lessons.title: Mitosis
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Mitosis For?

Mitosis is involved in growth, repair and asexual reproduction. Mitosis is needed for growth because new cells are formed by it and the body grows.

Stages of Mitosis

StageWhat happens
ProphaseChromosomes appear and the nuclear membrane disappears. In animal cells the centrioles separate and move towards the poles.
MetaphaseThe chromosomes come in a row and line up at the equator of the cell.
AnaphaseThe chromatids separate and move towards the poles.
TelophaseThe chromatids reach the poles and their movement stops. The nuclear membrane forms again (reappears).

After these stages, by cytokinesis the cytoplasm divides and the cell divides into two parts.

Points to Remember

  • In telophase the nuclear membrane reappears — saying it disappears in telophase is wrong; it disappears in prophase.
  • The stage in which chromatids reach the poles and their movement stops is telophase.
  • Separation of centrioles in animal cells takes place in prophase.

mcqs.q: Mitosis is involved in .........
mcqs.why: Mitosis is involved in growth, repair and asexual reproduction, because it makes new body cells. Gametes are produced by meiosis, not mitosis.

mcqs.q: In metaphase of mitosis .........
options: the chromosomes line up at the equator
mcqs.why: In metaphase the chromosomes come in a row at the equator of the cell. Reaching the poles happens later, in telophase.

mcqs.q: What happens during prophase of mitosis in animal cells?
options: Chromosomes line up at the equator
mcqs.why: In prophase the centrioles separate and move towards the poles in animal cells, while the chromosomes appear and the nuclear membrane disappears.

mcqs.q: The stage of mitosis in which chromatids reach the poles and their movement stops is .........
mcqs.why: In telophase the chromatids reach the poles and their movement stops, and the nuclear membrane forms again around them.

mcqs.q: Choose the odd one out.
mcqs.why: 'Telophase — cell membrane disappears' is the odd one out because it is wrong: in telophase the nuclear membrane reappears, it does not disappear. The other three pairs are correct.

mcqs.q: Why is mitosis needed for growth?
options: Because it halves the chromosome number
Because new cells are formed by it and the body grows
mcqs.why: Mitosis is needed for growth because new cells are formed by it and the body grows. Halving of chromosomes and gamete formation belong to meiosis.

mcqs.q: In anaphase of mitosis .........
options: the chromatids separate and move towards the poles
the chromosomes appear for the first time
mcqs.why: In anaphase the chromatids separate and move towards the poles. They reach the poles in telophase, after which cytokinesis divides the cell.

mcqs.q: The correct order of the stages of mitosis is .........
mcqs.why: Mitosis runs in the order prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase, and then cytokinesis divides the cell into two parts.

mcqs.q: After telophase, the cell divides into two parts by .........
mcqs.why: After the stages of mitosis, cytokinesis divides the cytoplasm and the cell divides into two parts, each with its own nucleus.

mcqs.q: In prophase of mitosis .........
options: chromosomes line up at the equator
chromosomes appear and the nuclear membrane disappears
mcqs.why: In prophase the chromosomes appear and the nuclear membrane disappears. Lining up at the equator is metaphase, and reaching the poles is telophase.

lessons.title: Apoptosis and Necrosis — the Two Paths of Cell Death
lessons.notes_html:
Two Paths of Cell Death

Cells can die in two different ways: apoptosis and necrosis.

Apoptosis — Organised Self-Destruction

Apoptosis is the sequence of changes by which a cell kills itself. It is the process in which a cell ends itself in an organised way — the organised self-destruction of a cell.

Necrosis — Death by External Factors

Necrosis is the death of cells caused by external factors. Unlike apoptosis, it is a disorderly death, not a planned one.

Apoptosis vs Necrosis

PointApoptosisNecrosis
What it isThe organised self-destruction of a cell; the cell kills itselfThe death of cells caused by external factors
MannerOrganised and plannedDisorderly
CauseThe cell's own sequence of changesExternal factors acting on the cell

mcqs.q: The sequence of changes by which a cell kills itself is called .........
mcqs.why: Apoptosis is the process in which a cell ends itself in an organised way. Necrosis, in contrast, is death caused by external factors.

mcqs.q: Death of cells caused by external factors is called .........
mcqs.why: Necrosis is the death of cells caused by external factors. Apoptosis is self-destruction carried out by the cell itself in an organised way.

mcqs.q: Apoptosis is best described as .........
options: death caused by injury from outside
the organised self-destruction of a cell
mcqs.why: Apoptosis is the organised self-destruction of a cell: the cell follows its own sequence of changes and ends itself in an orderly manner.

mcqs.q: Which statement is correct?
options: Apoptosis is disorderly, necrosis is organised
Necrosis is the death of cells caused by external factors
Apoptosis is caused by external factors
Both are types of cell division
mcqs.why: Necrosis is the disorderly death of cells caused by external factors, while apoptosis is the organised self-destruction of a cell. Neither is a type of division.

mcqs.q: A cell that ends itself in an organised way is showing .........
mcqs.why: Ending itself in an organised way is apoptosis. In necrosis the cell dies in a disorderly way because of external factors, not by its own programme.

mcqs.q: The main difference between apoptosis and necrosis is .........
options: apoptosis is organised self-destruction, necrosis is death caused by external factors
apoptosis happens in plants, necrosis in animals
apoptosis makes gametes, necrosis makes spores
mcqs.why: Apoptosis is the organised self-destruction of a cell, whereas necrosis is the disorderly death of cells caused by external factors.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT apoptosis?
options: A cell killing itself by a set sequence of changes
A cell ending itself in an organised way
Death of cells caused by external factors
mcqs.why: Death of cells caused by external factors is necrosis, not apoptosis. Apoptosis is always the cell's own organised self-destruction.

mcqs.q: Necrosis is a ......... death of cells.
mcqs.why: Necrosis is a disorderly death of cells caused by external factors. The planned and organised path of cell death is apoptosis.

mcqs.q: If a group of cells dies because of an external factor acting on them, the process is .........
mcqs.why: Death caused by external factors is necrosis. Apoptosis would be the cells destroying themselves in an organised way from inside.

mcqs.q: Apoptosis takes place through .........
options: a sequence of changes by which the cell kills itself
mcqs.why: Apoptosis works through a sequence of changes by which the cell kills itself in an organised way; external factors are the cause in necrosis instead.

lessons.title: Meiosis — Reduction Division
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Meiosis?

Meiosis is the type of cell division in which the chromosome number becomes half. In organisms, meiosis produces gametes. A spore mother cell also produces spores by meiosis. Meiosis does not produce somatic (body) cells.

Why Meiosis I Is Called Reduction Division

Meiosis I is called reduction division because in it the number of chromosomes becomes half. The chromosome number stays constant generation after generation because in meiosis the number becomes half and in fertilisation it becomes full again.

Two Divisions of Meiosis

DivisionStages
Meiosis IProphase I, metaphase I, anaphase I, telophase I
Meiosis IIProphase II, metaphase II, anaphase II, telophase II

In the end, four gametes are formed with half the number of chromosomes. No interphase occurs between meiosis I and meiosis II, because there is no need to copy DNA again; the chromosomes go directly into the second division.

Sub-stages of Prophase I

Prophase I has five sub-stages: leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis.

Term / Sub-stageWhat happens
BivalentA pair of homologous chromosomes formed in meiosis
PachyteneChromosomes thicken and crossing over takes place
ChiasmataThe points where homologous chromosomes meet each other and crossing over takes place
DiakinesisThe last stage of prophase I; chromosomes thicken further and the nuclear membrane disappears

More Events of Meiosis
